title: DreamBooth
summary: Teach a diffusion model to place your own subject in new scenes while preserving its identity.
task: Personalize a text-to-image model from 5–10 photographs, then generate the subject in unseen settings and styles.
model: Stable Diffusion 1.5 with LoRA in U-Net attention; frozen VAE and text encoder. Optional prior preservation.
training_data: 5–10 photographs of one subject, with varied views and backgrounds; keep related photo sessions in the same split.
evaluation_data: Held-out subject photos and a fixed prompt suite; compare the base model and adapter with identical seeds.

metrics.name: DINO-I ↑
metrics.meaning: Subject similarity to held-out reference photos.

metrics.name: CLIP-I ↑
metrics.meaning: Visual similarity to the reference subject.

metrics.name: CLIP-T ↑
metrics.meaning: Agreement between the generated image and its prompt.

deliverables: A reusable LoRA adapter and its training configuration.
A gallery of the same subject in several new scenes.
A baseline-versus-adapter comparison with fixed prompts and seeds.
An error analysis covering identity drift and overfitting.
context: DreamBooth learns a subject from a small image collection. The course implements a lightweight SD 1.5 LoRA variant; SDXL and FLUX are separate extension targets requiring their own training setup.

title: Textual Inversion
summary: Represent a personal visual concept with a new token that can be reused in text prompts.
task: Learn one embedding for a new concept token, then combine it with unfamiliar scenes and descriptions.
model: Stable Diffusion 1.5 with one trainable CLIP token embedding; the diffusion model and other embeddings stay frozen.
training_data: 5–10 photographs of one subject; reserve separate validation and test images before training.
evaluation_data: Held-out photographs and matched baseline/personalized generations using identical prompts, seeds and sampling settings.

metrics.name: DINO-I ↑
metrics.meaning: Similarity of the generated subject to reference photos.

metrics.name: CLIP-I ↑
metrics.meaning: Visual consistency with the learned concept.

metrics.name: CLIP-T ↑
metrics.meaning: Prompt alignment, measured using the ordinary text description.

deliverables: A learned embedding that reloads into the base model.
A prompt gallery showing the concept in different contexts.
A baseline comparison and a discussion of identity versus flexibility.

papers.title: An Image is Worth One Word: Textual Inversion

context: Textual inversion stores personalization in an embedding rather than a diffusion-model adapter. SDXL or FLUX experiments require a separate implementation beyond the course's SD 1.5 trainer.

title: Weapon Detection & Blur
summary: Detect firearms in images or film clips and blur the detected regions automatically.
task: Adapt a pretrained detector to one firearm class, choose a confidence threshold and apply blur to its predicted boxes.
model: COCO-pretrained YOLOv10S with a trainable detection head; the course trains both detection branches.
training_data: Firearm-related action recognition and object detection data, converted to YOLO boxes; include negative frames without weapons.
evaluation_data: Held-out videos or scenes, with all related frames kept together; use separate clips to demonstrate blur.

metrics.name: mAP@50:95 ↑
metrics.meaning: Detection quality across several box-overlap thresholds.

metrics.name: Miss rate ↓
metrics.meaning: Fraction of annotated firearms the detector misses.

metrics.name: False positive rate ↓
metrics.meaning: Fraction of weapon-free frames with at least one detection.

metrics.name: Latency ↓
metrics.meaning: Processing time measured on the chosen hardware and pipeline.

deliverables: A trained detector with a validation-selected threshold.
An image or video demo with detected objects blurred.
A test report covering misses, false alarms and processing speed.
Examples of difficult scenes, small objects and occlusion.

papers.title: Firearm-related action recognition and object detection dataset

context: YOLOv10 is the reference real-time detection family. Its COCO benchmark scores describe general object detection; firearm accuracy and film-domain transfer must be measured separately.

title: Text-to-SQL with LoRA
summary: Turn natural-language questions and a database schema into SQL queries that return the right answer.
task: Fine-tune a small code model, execute its SQL in an isolated SQLite evaluation database and compare results with reference queries.
model: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct with LoRA on attention q/v projections.
training_data: b-mc2/sql-create-context: question, schema and reference SQL triples, split by schema before training.
evaluation_data: Held-out schemas plus separate populated SQLite fixtures. Empty tables cannot establish execution accuracy.

metrics.name: Execution accuracy ↑
metrics.meaning: Generated and reference queries return the same result on populated fixtures.

metrics.name: Valid SQL ↑
metrics.meaning: Fraction of queries that execute within the evaluator's limits.

metrics.name: Exact match ↑
metrics.meaning: Textual agreement with reference SQL; not a proof of semantic equivalence.

metrics.name: Execution coverage ↑
metrics.meaning: Fraction of examples with usable fixtures and valid reference queries.

deliverables: A LoRA adapter and repeatable inference script.
A small SQLite database with held-out questions and populated fixtures.
A baseline-versus-LoRA execution report.
An analysis of joins, aggregation, sorting and invalid queries.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

context: LoRA changes a small set of trainable parameters while retaining a pretrained code model. The key experiment is executable SQL on unseen schemas; general language-model benchmark rankings do not measure this task.

title: Structured JSON with LoRA
summary: Adapt a language model to produce valid JSON that obeys a supplied schema.
task: Train on validated prompt/schema/answer examples and test whether freely generated outputs satisfy unseen schemas.
model: Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct with LoRA; free generation makes the effect of training measurable.
training_data: Curated prompt, JSON Schema and valid answer triples. Group related schemas before creating train and validation splits.
evaluation_data: Held-out schema families and a documented JSONSchemaBench subset. JSONSchemaBench provides schemas, not ready-made supervised answers.

metrics.name: Schema adherence ↑
metrics.meaning: Fraction of all outputs that pass the supplied JSON Schema.

metrics.name: Valid JSON ↑
metrics.meaning: Strictly parseable JSON without Markdown wrappers or invalid values.

metrics.name: Exact match ↑
metrics.meaning: Canonical JSON equality where a reference answer exists.

metrics.name: Capability retention
metrics.meaning: Optional before/after comparison on a fixed general-task evaluation set.

deliverables: A reloadable LoRA adapter and validated training data.
An evaluator for syntax, schema adherence and reference answers.
A comparison with the base model on unseen schemas.
An error gallery for nested objects, arrays and required fields.

papers.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

context: Schema adherence and task correctness are separate: a valid object can still contain the wrong answer. Constrained decoding is an optional comparison; the course baseline evaluates the learned model's unconstrained outputs.

title: Music-to-Image
summary: Convert a music excerpt into visual conditioning and generate an image that matches its mood or content.
task: Train an audio-conditioning adapter that connects a frozen audio encoder to a frozen diffusion model.
model: CLAP audio encoder → trainable MLP → eight conditioning tokens for Stable Diffusion 1.5.
training_data: MUImage music–image pairs, using the music as input; group related source songs and images before splitting.
evaluation_data: Held-out source groups and an external final test; use matched seeds and an empty-text diffusion baseline.

metrics.name: CLIP-I ↑
metrics.meaning: Similarity between generated and paired reference images; not direct audio–image alignment.

metrics.name: LPIPS diversity ↑
metrics.meaning: Variation across different seeds for the same music excerpt.

metrics.name: Human preference ↑
metrics.meaning: Blind listener preference for how well an image matches the music.

metrics.name: FID ↓
metrics.meaning: Optional image-distribution comparison on a sufficiently large test set.

deliverables: An audio-conditioning adapter and inference demo.
A gallery pairing music excerpts with generated images.
A matched comparison against the empty-text baseline.
A listener study and analysis of audio–visual consistency.
context: SonicDiffusion motivates audio-conditioned diffusion; MUImage supplies paired media. The course uses a smaller MLP adapter architecture. Ordinary CLIP cannot directly score audio, so semantic alignment also needs a listener evaluation.

title: Object Removal
summary: Remove a selected object and reconstruct a plausible background inside its mask.
task: Adapt an inpainting model using aligned images with and without an object, then preserve the original pixels outside the removal mask.
model: Stable Diffusion inpainting with LoRA in U-Net attention; frozen VAE and text encoder.
training_data: Licensed input/mask/clean-target triples, separated by scene. Clearly labelled synthetic pairs can support initial experiments.
evaluation_data: Held-out scenes and RemovalBench as a separate test benchmark; include the object's shadow or reflection in the mask when needed.

metrics.name: Masked MAE ↓
metrics.meaning: Pixel error inside the edited region against the clean target.

metrics.name: Masked PSNR ↑
metrics.meaning: Reconstruction quality inside the removal mask.

metrics.name: Outside-mask MAE ↓
metrics.meaning: Preservation of untouched pixels; compositing makes this zero by construction.

metrics.name: Visual review
metrics.meaning: Check object remnants, seams, invented objects, shadows and reflections.

deliverables: A saved inpainting model and mask-based editing demo.
Before/after examples with visible removal masks.
A baseline comparison on held-out paired scenes.
An error analysis of difficult backgrounds and object effects.

papers.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models

context: Latent diffusion provides the inpainting foundation; OmniEraser studies removal together with object effects. The local course evaluator measures masked reconstruction and does not reproduce RemovalBench's official semantic scoring.

title: Automatic Lyrics Transcription
summary: Adapt speech recognition to recover lyrics from singing recordings.
task: Fine-tune Whisper on aligned singing excerpts and compare transcription accuracy with the pretrained model.
model: Whisper large-v3-turbo with LoRA on q/v projections; full fine-tuning of a smaller Whisper is an optional experiment.
training_data: M4Singer Mandarin singing clips with verified Chinese text, language labels and song IDs; each aligned excerpt is at most 30 seconds.
evaluation_data: Song-disjoint validation and test sets, keeping all versions of a composition in one split; add formatting labels only when available.

metrics.name: CER ↓
metrics.meaning: Character error rate, the main metric for the Mandarin course dataset.

metrics.name: WER ↓
metrics.meaning: Word error rate under an explicitly documented tokenization rule.

metrics.name: Formatting F1 ↑
metrics.meaning: Punctuation, line and section boundaries when corresponding reference labels exist.

metrics.name: Runtime ↓
metrics.meaning: Transcription time and memory under fixed hardware and decoding settings.

deliverables: A saved Whisper adapter and transcription pipeline.
Audio/text examples comparing the baseline and adapted model.
A song-disjoint CER/WER report.
An analysis of accompaniment, pronunciation and phrase boundaries.

papers.title: Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision

context: Whisper is the speech-recognition foundation; WhisperMSS is a reference for adapting pretrained models to Mandarin singing. General speech benchmark scores should not be treated as expected lyrics-transcription performance.

title: Hair Segmentation & Sharpening
summary: Predict a hair mask and increase sharpness only within the selected region.
task: Adapt a segmentation decoder to hair, then apply masked unsharp enhancement: image + α × (image − blurred image).
model: SAM 1 ViT-B with a trainable mask decoder; frozen image and prompt encoders, using a full-image box.
training_data: LaPa portraits and semantic hair labels; use verified identity groups where available and document the split protocol.
evaluation_data: Held-out portrait images and masks, with separate inspection of fine hair boundaries and the final sharpened output.

metrics.name: IoU ↑
metrics.meaning: Overlap between the predicted and reference hair regions.

metrics.name: Dice / F1 ↑
metrics.meaning: Balance of missed hair pixels and false positives.

metrics.name: Boundary F1 ↑
metrics.meaning: Accuracy near hair contours under a stated pixel tolerance.

metrics.name: Precision / Recall ↑
metrics.meaning: Leakage into the background versus missing parts of the hair.

deliverables: A trained hair-mask decoder and inference pipeline.
Portrait, predicted mask and selectively sharpened result examples.
A segmentation report and boundary error analysis.
A comparison of enhancement strengths and visible artifacts.

papers.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos
A New Dataset and Boundary-Attention Semantic Segmentation for Face Parsing

context: SAM supplies pretrained segmentation features, but hair semantics must be learned for this task. The executable course baseline uses SAM 1; SAM 2/2.1 is a separate extension requiring implementation and measurement.

title: Portrait Bokeh
summary: Keep a portrait subject sharp while softly blurring the background.
task: Predict foreground opacity and composite the portrait with a blurred copy: output = mask × image + (1 − mask) × blur(image).
model: SAM 1 ViT-B with a fine-tuned mask decoder and frozen encoders, followed by Gaussian background blur.
training_data: P3M-10k portrait images and alpha annotations; group related people, source images and sessions before splitting.
evaluation_data: Held-out portraits with alpha masks; assess opacity and binary segmentation separately, then inspect the final composites.

metrics.name: Opacity MAE ↓
metrics.meaning: Error in continuous foreground opacity against the reference alpha.

metrics.name: IoU / Dice ↑
metrics.meaning: Foreground agreement after thresholding the masks.

metrics.name: Boundary F1 ↑
metrics.meaning: Contour quality around hair, shoulders and fine details.

metrics.name: Visual review
metrics.meaning: Inspect halos, background leakage and blur around subject edges.

deliverables: A saved portrait-mask decoder and adjustable blur demo.
Original, opacity mask and bokeh result examples.
A baseline-versus-tuned segmentation and opacity report.
An analysis of fine hair, multiple subjects and edge artifacts.

papers.title: SAM 2: Segment Anything in Images and Videos

context: Portrait matting motivates careful treatment of soft boundaries. This course baseline approximates bokeh with a SAM 1 opacity mask and Gaussian blur; depth-aware optics and SAM 2 adaptation are optional extensions.
